messages.author: 5b9f4c138fd9a813
messages.subject: some doubts about procD.lm
parts:
Hi all,

I think I might have a problem. When I use shapiro.test, I see that my coords or shape data has a non-normal distribuition, but Csize (size) is normally distributed. So, in this case, I can''t use procD.lm to test the interaction of shape and the environmental factors that I have, is that correct? If this situation is true, is there something that I can use to test my hypothesis?

Again, I am attaching my data and scripts.

Gratefully, 

Diniz F.

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] some doubts about procD.lm
parts:
A quick comment. First, shapiro.test is generally univariate, and what matters for shape is multivariate.  Second, it is the distribution of residuals that matters more than the y variates. Finally, permutations can be rather robust to deviations of normality when present.

Dean

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] some doubts about procD.lm
parts:
As a follow up to Dean’s comment, if a matrix or array is used for the shapiro.test function, it will “vectorize” it; i.e., it converts a p x k x n array into an npk x 1 vector.  It would be incorrect to assume such a vector comprises normally distributed values.

The plot.procD.lm function can help evaluate normality and homoscedasticity of residuals in a multivariate-friendly way, but is not a formal test.

Mike
